prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2001 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core purpose and governance
- Independence is central: more SNP MPs strengthen the case for a referendum; a majority of SNP MPs would trigger one. SNP MPs will always put Scotland first and seek more powers for the Scottish Parliament.
- Create a written constitution; inclusive citizenship; retain the monarchy subject to a referendum; proportional representation at all levels; reduce and democratise quangos; support the civil service in an independent Scotland.

Fiscal strategy and investment
- Use Scotland’s wealth for Scotland through:
  - Scottish Fund for Future Generations: invest surplus oil revenues in a sovereign fund to finance public services sustainably.
  - Scottish Trust for Public Investment (STPI): a not‑for‑profit vehicle to finance infrastructure at lower cost than PFI/PPP.
- Taxation: no increase in overall tax burden without a mandate; launch a comprehensive tax review to make taxes fairer and simpler and cut business taxes. Immediate 10p/gallon fuel duty cut funded by a new 5p income tax band over £100,000. Review local government finance, including local income tax.

Education and young people
- Abolish tuition fees; rebuild maintenance grants.
- Establish an Education Convention; cap P1–P3 classes at 18; end league tables; major school refurbishment via STPI; support Gaelic medium education; protect rural schools; strengthen inclusion and teacher support.
- Vote at 16; implement UNCRC; create a Children’s Commissioner.

Economy, jobs, and tourism
- Target full employment via infrastructure (road/rail/air/ports/digital broadband), reskilling, and more responsive enterprise agencies.
- Tourism: shift to aggressive marketing, better access and transport links, and a Scottish gateway airport.

Work, pay, and unions
- Devolve and redesign the New Deal; raise the minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages; statutory Charter of Trade Union Rights; support EU worker protections.

Environment, energy, and water
- State of the Nation Environmental Audit and National Environment Plan.
- By 2010: 12% of total energy and 25% of electricity from renewables; no new nuclear; lead in decommissioning; apply precautionary and polluter‑pays principles; strengthen SEPA oversight (including MoD).
- Water: halt steep charge rises; more democratic governance; protect low‑income users.

Health and care
- Create a National Health Care Commission to set strategy and end postcode treatment; HTBS guidance binding.
- Prevention: free fruit in primary schools; nutritional standards for school meals.
- Free dental check‑ups; freeze/review prescription charges.
- Invest via STPI; equipment audit; hospital cleanliness fund; recruit at least 1,500 nurses; halve inpatient waiting times; free personal care for the elderly.

Europe, defence, and international
- Pro‑EU, pro‑subsidiarity, anti‑superstate; euro only with the right conditions and a referendum.
- Remove Trident from Scotland; oppose US missile defence; phased withdrawal from NATO while maintaining conventional cooperation; form a professional Scottish Defence Force.
- External affairs focused on trade/tourism; meet UN aid targets, cancel debt, untie aid.

Culture, sport, and languages
- Devolve broadcasting oversight; push a “Scottish Six” and digital rollout.
- Prioritise community sport; football academies and Euro 2008 bid.
- Reform arts funding; establish a national theatre and Scottish Lottery.
- Secure status for Gaelic; strengthen Scots language teaching and media.

Social justice, housing, and law
- National Anti‑Poverty Strategy; end asylum vouchers; fast and fair assessments.
- Press UK to assume historic council housing debt; devolve housing benefit; invest via STPI; oppose wholesale stock transfer; stable core funding for voluntary sector; tackle homelessness.
- Extend Disability Discrimination Act; disability equality indicator.
- Drugs: tougher on dealers; drug courts and rehabilitation.
- Policing and justice: £25m for 1,000 extra officers; parental compensation orders for youth damage; lifelong restriction orders for high‑risk sex offenders; speed up courts; retain fine revenues in Scotland.

Rural, agriculture, fisheries, and land
- Cut fuel duty; small business rates relief; improve rural transport and broadband; protect post offices, schools and links; contingency support for crises.
- Post–FMD agricultural review; fair EU implementation; support LFAs; promote diversification and quality exports.
- Fisheries: compensated tie‑ups, stronger conservation, devolved management via zonal councils, restore Scottish jurisdiction; salmon farming inquiry.
- Empower community land rights; national freshwater fisheries policy.

Pensions and social security
- Restore the earnings link using NI surplus; narrow the MIG/pension gap; spread winter fuel payments weekly and extend to severely disabled.
- Create a single benefits agency; simplify housing benefit; improve take‑up; smoother transitions for disabled people and carers.

Transport
- Secure a fair UK funding share; create Regional Transport Authorities and a single safety regulator; take a public stake in Railtrack.
- Reopen and electrify key lines (e.g., Borders, airport links); national concessionary travel; targeted road upgrades; reduce ferry fares and pilot Road Equivalent Tariff; expand direct flights; abolish Skye Bridge tolls.
